item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 places plastocyanin/azurin-like proteins, ephrin ectodomains, and the N-terminal domain of peptidylarginine deiminase PAD4 together only as remote members of the same all-beta cupredoxin-like structural/evolutionary grouping: class b, fold b.6 Cupredoxin-like, superfamily b.6.1 Cupredoxins. They are separated into different families: Plastocyanin/azurin-like is b.6.1.1, Ephrin ectodomain is b.6.1.5, and PAD4 N-terminal domain is b.6.1.6. Thus SCOPe supports a shared cupredoxin-type superfamily/fold relationship, not close family-level homology or shared biological role. Copper binding and electron-transfer function should not be transferred from plastocyanin/azurin to ephrin ectodomains or PAD4 N-terminal domains on this basis.
